Content:
The region [MATH: R] is a type II region. So, our first task is to fully describe this region.

Content:
We start by drawing an arrow parallel to the [MATH: x]-axis that

Content:

So, our solid can be written as the type II region

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 5-y-z \big\},]

where

[MATH: D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 2 \big\}]

is the projection of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: yz]-plane, shown below.

Content:
[MATH: \iiint \limits_{R} 2y \: \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{5-y-z} 2y \: \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A]

A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: u_1(y,z) \leq x \leq u_2(y,z) \big\}.]

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If [MATH: R] is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] over [MATH: R] as a mixed integral, as follows:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm{d}x \right]\,\textrm d A]

In our case, we have

[MATH: u_1(y,z) = -2, \qquad u_2(y,z) = ye^{z+2}.]

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as [MATH: \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{-2}^{ye^{z+2}} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A.]

Now, the region [MATH: D] is given by [MATH: D =\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 4, \: -y^2 \leq z \leq \sqrt{y} \right\}.]

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over [MATH: D] as a repeated integral, we get [MATH: ∬_(D)[∫_{− 2}^{ye^{z + 2}}f(x, y, z)dx]dA|= ∫_{1}^{4}∫_{− y^{2}}^{sqrt(y)}[∫_{− 2}^{ye^{z + 2}}f(x, y, z)dx]dzdy; = ∫_{1}^{4}∫_{− y^{2}}^{sqrt(y)}∫_{− 2}^{ye^{z + 2}}f(x, y, z)dxdzdy.]

Content:

Content:

Content:
[MATH: \iiint \limits_{R} 2y \: \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{5-y-z} 2y \: \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A]

Content:
Now, since the region [MATH: D] is a type I plane region, we can express the region [MATH: R] as

Content:
[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 5-y-z \big\},]

Content:
and therefore, our mixed integral can be written as the following repeated integral:

Content:
[MATH: \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{5-x-z} 2y \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A

Content:
Evaluating this using the usual methods, we get

Content:
[MATH: \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{5-y-z} 2y \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{64}{3}.]
